               <ns0:p n="1">1 WE then, <ns0:hi>as</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Cor. 3.9.</ns0:note> workers together <ns0:hi>with him</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Ministers of the Gospel are Fellow workers together with Christ; though but as Instruments, serving him as the Principal Agent, and efficient Cause: He trod the Wine-press of his Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thers wrath alone, and had no Partner in the Purchace of mans salvation; but in the application of the purchased salvation, he admits of Fellow-workers. Though the internal work be his alone, and the effects of his Spirit upon the Souls of those whose hearts are changed; yet there is a Ministerial part, which lyeth in <ns0:hi>Exhortation</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Argument,</ns0:hi> by the Ear conveyed to the Soul; thus Ministers work <ns0:hi>together with Christ.</ns0:hi> And without him they can do nothing: They are Workers, but they must have Christ work with them, or they will find that they labour in vain.</ns0:note>, beseech <ns0:hi>you</ns0:hi> also <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Heb. 12.15.</ns0:note>, that ye re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceive not the grace of God in vain <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Grace signifieth any free Gift; and 'tis in the New Testament variously applied; but here it signifies, the <ns0:hi>Doctrine of the Gospel,</ns0:hi> held forth in the Preaching of it; which these <ns0:hi>Corinthians</ns0:hi> had received with the Ears of their Bodies. And this was <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi>'s, and should be every godly Minister's work, not with roughness, but with all mildness and gentleness, to beseech those to whom they preach the Gospel, that they would believe and embrace it, and live up to the holy Rules of it; without which (as to their Souls benefit) all the kindness of God, in affording them the Gospel and means of Grace, is in vain and lost; (though God yet hath his End, and his Ministers shall be a <ns0:hi>sweet savour to God,</ns0:hi> as well with reference to them that pe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rish, as those who shall be saved). For the effectual Grace of God in the heart, that cannot be received in vain; nor is that here spoken of.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="2">2 For he saith, I have heard thee in a time ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cepted, and in the day of salvation have I succour<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed thee <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">The words here quoted, are taken out of the Prophet <ns0:hi>I<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />saiah,</ns0:hi> 49.8. according to the <ns0:hi>Septuagint</ns0:hi>'s Translation. Though some think, that the Apostle here doth but accommodate to the Spiritual Salvation brought in by Christ, a temporal Salvati<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on mentioned, and primarily intended; yet the most and best Interpreters rather judge, that whole Chapter in <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> to refer to Christ, and that the <ns0:hi>Salvation</ns0:hi> there mentioned, is to be un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />derstood of the Spiritual Salvation of the Gospel; of which also the Apostle speaketh here, and maketh these words (as in the Prophet) the words of God the Father to Christ his Son, testifying both his assistance of him in the accomplishment of the work of mans redemption, and his acceptance of him; Ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cording to which sense, the <ns0:hi>Accepted time</ns0:hi> is the same with what the Apostle calls, <ns0:hi>The fulness of time</ns0:hi>; (though it may also be so called in the same sense that the Apostle calleth the <ns0:hi>Gospel</ns0:hi> a <ns0:hi>faithful Saying, worthy of all acceptation,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 1.15.) in which sense the Gospel-time was prophesied of as an <ns0:hi>acceptable time, Gen.</ns0:hi> 49.10. <ns0:hi>Haggai</ns0:hi> 1.8.</ns0:note>: behold, now <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> the accepted time, be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hold, now <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> the day of salvation <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Now is that <ns0:hi>accepted,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>acceptable time,</ns0:hi> now is that day of salvation spoken of by the Prophet; therefore you are concerned to receive this Grace of the Gospel, and to live up to the Rule of it.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="3">3 Giving no offence in any thing <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">To <ns0:hi>give no offence</ns0:hi> signifies to avoid all actions which may be occasion of spiritual stumbling unto others, <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> to make them to sin against God, or estrange their hearts from Christ, and the owning and profession of his Gospel. These words may be understood as a general Precept given to all Christians; So it agreeth with 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 10.30, 32. or (which the following Ver<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ses seem most to favour) as referring to himself and <ns0:hi>Timothy,</ns0:hi> and other Ministers of the Gospel; like true Pastors of the Church of Christ, going out before the Flock, and shewing in their Example what they ought to be.</ns0:note>, that the mi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nistry be not blamed <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">The Ministry here may either signifie the <ns0:hi>Office of the Ministry,</ns0:hi> or the <ns0:hi>Subject</ns0:hi> of it, the Gospel, which, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 5.18. is called the Ministry of Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />conciliation; not only the Office of the Ministry, but the Gos<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pel it self, suffereth by the scandalous conversation of Ministers and private Christians; ignorant persons being not able, or not willing, to distinguish betwixt the faults of persons, and the faults of a Doctrine or Office.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="4">4 But in all things <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                     <ns0:hi>Gr. com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mending, Chap.</ns0:hi> 4.2.</ns0:note> approving our selves <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Cor. 4.1.</ns0:note> as the ministers of God <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Ministers of the Gospel are in the first place to be consi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dered as the <ns0:hi>Ministers of God,</ns0:hi> secondarily as Ministers and Servants of the Church; which they ought to serve so far, as in serving it they do obey Christ. None can approve, or com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mend themselves for Ministers of God that live a scandalous life: God hath not sent them to lay stumbling blocks in, but to remove them out of the way of men.</ns0:note>, in much patience <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Patience</ns0:hi> signifies an enduring of Evils, quietly and cheerfully, at the command of God; or when we see it is the Will of God, we should patient<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly submit to put our necks into the heaviest Yokes. The Apo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stle goes on reckoning up several <ns0:hi>Species</ns0:hi> of those Evils:</ns0:note>, in afflictions <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Af<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fliction</ns0:hi> is a general term signifying any Evils that wear out our Bodies.</ns0:note>, in necessities <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Necessities</ns0:hi> signifie any bodily wants of food, or rai<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment, or whatever is for the use of mans life.</ns0:note>, in distresses <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Distresses</ns0:hi> sig<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nifie properly a man's being straitned, or thrust up in a place, so as that he knoweth not how to steer himself; and, Metapho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rically, a want of counsel, not knowing what to do, or which way to turn our selves.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="5">5 In stripes <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">The Apostle. <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 11.23. tells us he was in <ns0:hi>stripes often</ns0:hi>; and <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 24. that of <ns0:hi>the Iews</ns0:hi> he <ns0:hi>five times received forty stripes save one</ns0:hi>: we read of his <ns0:hi>many stripes,</ns0:hi> 23.</ns0:note>, in imprisonments <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Of the im<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />prisonment of him, and <ns0:hi>Silas, Act.</ns0:hi> 26. (which was not the only time before the writing of this Epistle, as appeareth by this Verse.)</ns0:note>, in <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                     <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> in tos<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sings to and fro.</ns0:note> tu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mults <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Tumults,</ns0:hi> or Seditions raised by the Jews and the Heathens; we have a Record of one at <ns0:hi>Ephesus, Acts</ns0:hi> 19. cau<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sed by <ns0:hi>Demetrius</ns0:hi>; Others, by Tumults here, understand un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fixed and incertain habitations, tossings to and fro, so, as they could be quiet in no place; but the former seemeth rather the sense of the Word, as <ns0:hi>Luke.</ns0:hi> 21.9. 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 14.33.</ns0:note>, in labours <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Labours,</ns0:hi> he either means labours with his hands; (which <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> was some<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />times put to, as <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 18.1, 2, 3. & 20.34.) Or travels, and journies. The word is a general word, significative of any pains that men take.</ns0:note>, in watchings <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">Religious watching, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 11.27.</ns0:note>, in fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stings <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">In <ns0:hi>fastings,</ns0:hi> as acts of Discipline, <ns0:hi>by which he kept under his body, and brought it under subjection</ns0:hi>; (as he told us, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 9.27.)</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="6">6 By pureness <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">As the Apostle in the former words had declared the <ns0:hi>pati<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ence</ns0:hi> of his conversation, in the enduring of the afflictions of the Gospel; so in this Verse he declares the more internal holiness of it, under the general Notion of <ns0:hi>pureness</ns0:hi>; shewed in his <ns0:hi>knowledge, faith, gentleness, kindness</ns0:hi> or goodness towards all men. The word translated <ns0:hi>pureness</ns0:hi> signifieth rather the universal rectitude of his heart and ways, than (as some think) the ha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bit or exercise of any particular vertue.</ns0:note>, by knowledge <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">In, or by, <ns0:hi>Know<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ledge</ns0:hi>; a right understanding and notion of spiritual things: if it doth not here signifie <ns0:hi>Faith,</ns0:hi> which is a Superstructure on this Foundation, and that habit which hath a special influence upon <ns0:hi>purifying the heart, Acts</ns0:hi> 15.9. Without knowledge there can be no purity, <ns0:hi>Prov.</ns0:hi> 19.2.</ns0:note>, by long suf<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fering <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">By <ns0:hi>long-suffering,</ns0:hi> the Apo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stle means not being easily provoked by such as had offended him, or done him wrong.</ns0:note>, by kindness <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">The word translated <ns0:hi>Kind<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness,</ns0:hi> signifies generally any goodness by which a man may shew himself either sweet and pleasant, or useful and profita<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ble unto his Neighbour.</ns0:note>, by the holy Ghost <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Thus the Apostle sheweth how he behaved himself; but not through his own strength, but through the influence and assistance of the Holy Ghost.</ns0:note>, by love unfeigned <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">The <ns0:hi>Love unfeigned</ns0:hi> here mentioned, is a general term signifying that habit of Grace wrought in his Soul by the holy Spirit of God, which was the Principle of the <ns0:hi>long-suffering</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>kindness</ns0:hi> before mentioned.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:465" />7 By the word of truth <ns0:note n="⸫" place="bottom">Living up to, and keeping our eye upon the Word of God, which is the Word of Truth: This seemeth to be the sense rather than speaking truth to every one, (as some have thought.)</ns0:note>, by <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Cor. 2.4.</ns0:note> the power of God <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">By the efficacious working of the Spirit of God upon our hearts, inabling us to live up to the Doctrine we preach. Some understand here, by the Power of God, that ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />traordinary Power of working Miracles, which God gave the Apostles; Others, the Gospel, which the Apostle calls the <ns0:hi>Power of God to Salvation, Rom.</ns0:hi> 1.16. It may be understood of the first and the last joined together; for the Gospel is no otherwise the Power of God to Salvation, than as it is attend<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed, to the Souls of those to whom it is so made powerful, with the inward, powerful, efficacious working of the holy Spirit.</ns0:note>, by the <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 10.4. Eph. 6.11, 13. 2 Tim. 4.7.</ns0:note> armour of righteousness, on the right hand, and on the left <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">By the <ns0:hi>Armour of Righteousness,</ns0:hi> he means a good Conscience, (which cannot be without an universal rectitude, or uprightness of life) which is a defence against all Tempta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tions, either from prosperity, or from adversity. In which sense that of <ns0:hi>Solomon</ns0:hi> is true, <ns0:hi>He that walketh uprightly, walk<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth safely,</ns0:hi> Prov. 10.9. and <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> prayeth, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 25.21. <ns0:hi>Let integrity and uprightness preserve me.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 By honour, and dishonour <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">We depart not from our integrity, whether we be honou<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />red, or dishonoured.</ns0:note>, by evil report, and good report <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Well or evilly reported of. This hath from the beginning been the lot of all the faithful Ministers of Christ; some have given them honour, others have cast re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />proach upon them; some have given a good report of them, some an evil report.</ns0:note>; as deceivers, and <ns0:hi>yet</ns0:hi> true <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Some have represented them as Im<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />postors, and such as deceived the people; others have spo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ken of them as true men: their business is to go through good report and bad report, honour and dishonour, still holding fall their integrity.</ns0:note>:</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 As unknown <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Dealt with by Jews and Heathens, as persons wholly un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />known to them, though we be sufficiently known.</ns0:note>, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 4.2.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:hi>yet</ns0:hi> well known <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Or be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing such whom the World knoweth not, as to our state to<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />wards God, and interest in him, though it knows us well e<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nough as to our other circumstances.</ns0:note>: as <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 4.10, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> dy<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing, and behold we live <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">So hunted and perse<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cuted, as that we appear every day dying; yet such hath been the Power of Gods Providence, that we yet live: And</ns0:note>: as chastened, and not killed <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">though our heavenly Father chasteneth us, yet we are not utterly con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sumed; the Apostle alludeth to that, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 118.18. <ns0:hi>The Lord hath chastened me sore, but he hath not given me over to death.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>:</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 As sorrowful, yet always rejoycing <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Appearing to others as persons drowned in griefs and sorrows, yet we are always rejoicing in God, (<ns0:hi>Hab.</ns0:hi> 3.17, 18.) and in the testimony of a good Conscience, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 1.12.</ns0:note>: as poor, <ns0:hi>yet</ns0:hi> making many rich <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">In outward appearance poor, having no abundance of the good things of this life; yet making many rich in Knowledge and Grace: God by us dispensing to them the Riches of his Grace.</ns0:note>: as having nothing, and yet possessing all things <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">As having nothing, no houses, no lands, no silver or gold, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 3.6. yet being as well satisfied and contented, as if all things were ours; as well satisfied with that little which we have, as the men of the World are with their abundance; possessing all things in Christ, though having little in the Crea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ture.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11 O ye Corinthians, our mouth is open unto you, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. 7.2, 3.</ns0:note> our heart is enlarged <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Our mouth is open to speak freely to you, and to com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />municate to you the whole Will and Counsel of God; our heart is <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> both by the Love that I have towards you, and by the <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> that i<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> have in you. This inlargement of my heart is that which openeth my lips, and makes me speak freely to you, both in admonishing you of your <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and in exhort<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing you to your duty.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 Ye are not straitned in us <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">If you cannot mutually rejoice in me, and what I write; or if you do not repay me the like affection, the fault is not in me; I have done my duty, and that too from a true Prin<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ciple of Love to you.</ns0:note>, but ye are strait<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ned in your own bowels <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">But it is through mistakes, and mis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />apprehensions in your selves, your not <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>right conceiving of me in the discharge of my Apostolical Office. Or the cause of your trouble and sorrow, is from your selves, upon your suffering the incestuous Person, and other scandalous persons, to abide in your Communion; which was an Errour I could not but take notice of, according to that Apostolical Autho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rity which God hath committed to me.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 Now for a recompence in the same, (<ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Cor. 4.14.</ns0:note> I speak as unto <ns0:hi>my</ns0:hi> children) be ye also enlarged <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Be ye also inlarged,</ns0:hi> both in <ns0:hi>Love to me,</ns0:hi> and also in <ns0:hi>Obedi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ence</ns0:hi>; it is but a just recompence for that great affection which I have born, and upon all occasions shewed to you; and also for that Faithfulness which I have shewed in discharging the duty of my relation to you. For I speak as a Father unto Children, it being but reasonable, that Children should recom<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pence to their Fathers their Love to them; and be as exact and faithful in their duty to their Parents, as their Parents are in their duty towards them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Deut. 7.2.</ns0:note> Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">They too much restrain the sense of this general Precept, who either limit it to Religious Communion with Idolaters, or to Civil Communion in Marriages. The Precept is deli<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vered in a term of more general significancy, than to be li<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mited by either of these; (though both of them questionless be comprehended in it) <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, do not be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />come such as in the same yoke draw another way. It is a Metaphor drawn from Horses or Oxen; which should draw together, being in the same yoke, neither standing still, nor yet holding back. It is a general Precept, prohibitive of all unnecessary communion and intimate fellowship with such, as either in matters of Faith, or Worship, or in their Lives and Conversations, declare themselves to be Unbelievers: (for why we should expound <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> of Infidels meerly, I cannot tell) especially considering, that the Apostle, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 5.9, 11. seems to allow a further communion with an Heathen, than with a notoriously scandalous Christian. So as this Precept may reasonably be interpreted by those in the former Epistle, of <ns0:hi>marrying with such, eating with them at Idol-feasts,</ns0:hi> or at the Lords Table, (as <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 5.) maintaining <ns0:hi>intimate Communion with them,</ns0:hi> &c.</ns0:note>: For <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Sam. 5.2, 3. 1 King. 18.21. 1 Cor. 10.21.</ns0:note> what fellowship hath righte<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ousness with unrighteousness? and what communi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on hath light with darkness <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">The reason he giveth, is, because they could have no comfortable communion with such; they were <ns0:hi>Righ<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />teousness</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> those persons were <ns0:hi>Vnrighteousness</ns0:hi>; they were <ns0:hi>Light,</ns0:hi> such persons were <ns0:hi>Darkness,</ns0:hi> that is, full of the darkness of sin and ignorance. In the mean time this Precept ought not to be extended to a total avoiding of Commerce with, or being in the Company of, either Heathens, or scandalous per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sons; for as to that, the <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ame Apostle had before determined it lawful, 1 <ns0:hi>Epist.</ns0:hi> 5.11. whatever Communion with such per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sons is either necessary from the Law of God, or Nature; or for the support and upholding of humane Life and Society, is lawful even with such persons; but all other is unlawful.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 And what concord hath Christ with Be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lial <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">By <ns0:hi>Belial</ns0:hi> in this Text, very good Interpreters understand the <ns0:hi>Devil</ns0:hi>; judging that the Apostle here opposeth <ns0:hi>Christ,</ns0:hi> who is the Head of <ns0:hi>Believers,</ns0:hi> and of the Church, to him who is the Head of all <ns0:hi>Vnbelievers,</ns0:hi> and the God of the World. The term is used only in this place in the New Testament, but ve<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry often in the Old Testament, to express men notoriously wicked and scandalous, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 13.13. <ns0:hi>Iudg.</ns0:hi> 19.22. 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 1.16<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> & 2.12. & 25.17. 2 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 16.7. 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 13.7. The Hebrews themselves are not agreed in the Etymology of it; <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 101.3. a wicked thing is called a <ns0:hi>thing of Belial</ns0:hi> (as may be seen in the Margents of our Bibles) so as the Argument is drawn from our duty of Conformity to our Head; Christ hath no fellowship with the Devil, therefore we ought to have no unnecessary communion with such who manifest themselves to be of their Father the Devil, by their doing his works; nor hath Christ any communion with the Sons of <ns0:hi>Belial.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>? or what part hath he that believeth with an infidel <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">What <ns0:hi>part</ns0:hi> or portion, that is, what society or communion hath a Believer with one that believeth not? What hath he to do with him? It was an usual Phrase amongst the Jews, <ns0:hi>Iosh.</ns0:hi> 22.25.27. Some by this <ns0:hi>part</ns0:hi> understand, what portion in the life to come: in which sense it teacheth us, that we should maintain intimate and elective communion in this life only with such, as we would gladly have our portion with in ano<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther life. But the most judicious Interpreters think this is not intended in this place.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 And what agreement hath the temple of God
<ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:466" />
with idols <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">This particular instance giveth some Expositors occasion to interpret <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 14. of communion with Idolaters in such Acts of Religion as are proper to them; but nothing hinders but that that Precept may be interpreted more generally, though the Apostle gives this as one particular instance, wherein he would have them avoid communion with Unbelievers.</ns0:note>? For ye <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Heb. 3.6.</ns0:note> are the temple of the li<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ving God <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">The Argument is drawn from what the Apostle had before asserted 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 3.16. & 6.19. their being the Temples of the Holy Ghost. Which he proveth from <ns0:hi>Lev.</ns0:hi> 26.12. <ns0:hi>Ezek.</ns0:hi> 37.26, 27.</ns0:note>, as God hath said, I will dwell in them, and walk in <ns0:hi>them,</ns0:hi> and I will be their God, and they shall be my people <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">Not that what the Apostle meaneth here, is the literal meaning of <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 26.11, 12. for it is manifest, that God by <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> there, is speaking not of Gods dwelling in the persons of Believers, or in his Church, but of that gracious presence and manifestation of himself to his People in the <ns0:hi>Tabernacle</ns0:hi> erected by his order. Some therefore think, that the place here alluded to, though not quoted <ns0:hi>verbatim,</ns0:hi> is, that <ns0:hi>Ezek.</ns0:hi> 37.26. which is a promise respecting the Kingdom of Christ; where God promi<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>eth to make a Covenant of Peace with his people, and saith, <ns0:hi>I will place them, and multiply them, and will set my Sanctuary in the midst of them for evermore: my Tabernacle also shall be with them, yea, I will be their God, and they shall be my people.</ns0:hi> The words, as they are here quoted, are intirely to be found in no one Text of holy Writ; it is sufficient that they are to be found there in parts. Nor doth this Text so properly speak of Gods dwelling in particular Believers, as of his dwelling in the Chur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ches of his People; therefore though he speaks of <ns0:hi>many, ye are,</ns0:hi> yet Temple is in the Singular Number. These <ns0:hi>many</ns0:hi> are but <ns0:hi>one body</ns0:hi>; the Church in which God dwelleth, and with which he hath Communion, which is expressed by <ns0:hi>walking in them</ns0:hi>; as in the <ns0:hi>Revelation,</ns0:hi> he is said to <ns0:hi>walk in the midst of the golden Candlesticks.</ns0:hi> Nor is the term <ns0:hi>living</ns0:hi> vainly added to <ns0:hi>God</ns0:hi>; for besides that he is usually so called, as being <ns0:hi>Ever living,</ns0:hi> and the Fountain of all Life; it also sheweth the opposition be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />twixt him and Idols, which are dead things: and therefore God could have no more Communion with Idols, than the <ns0:hi>li<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ving</ns0:hi> can have with the <ns0:hi>dead</ns0:hi>; nor could they have Commu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nion with the living God and dead Idols. Nor could they be the People of the living God, and the People or Worshippers of dead Idols; so as those that were Idolaters, must lose the advantage of that Covenant wherein God had said, <ns0:hi>I will be your God, and you shall be my people.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Rev. 18.4.</ns0:note> Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord, and touch not the unclean thing, and I will receive you <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">The Apostle here quoteth words out of the Old Testa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment, no where to be found there syllabically, without varia<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion; but keeping to the sense of them, (which is a thing very usual with the Penmen of the New Testament.) The first quotation seemeth to be taken from <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 52.11. <ns0:hi>Depart ye, depart ye, go ye out from thence, touch no unclean thing, go ye out of the midst of her, be ye clean that bear the Vessels of the Lord.</ns0:hi> Inter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />preters are not agreed, as to the <ns0:hi>Term</ns0:hi> from whence the Prophet there admonisheth the Jews to depart: Some make it to be their former sinful courses; others make it to be the Kingdom of the <ns0:hi>Devil</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Antichrist</ns0:hi>; others make it to be <ns0:hi>li<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />teral Babylon</ns0:hi>; the Prophet foreseeing, that when the Jews should have a liberty given them to leave <ns0:hi>Babylon,</ns0:hi> (which hap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pened in the time of <ns0:hi>Cyrus</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Persian</ns0:hi> Monarch) some of them (now as it were incorporated with the <ns0:hi>Chaldeans</ns0:hi>) would lin<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ger and find a difficulty to pluck up their stakes in <ns0:hi>Babylon,</ns0:hi> though it were in order to their return to <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> hereto<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore the joy and praise of the whole Earth. Whatever was the Prophets meaning, certain it is, the Apostolical Precept cannot be interpreted of a leaving <ns0:hi>literal Babylon,</ns0:hi> for neither the Christian Jews, or Gentiles, were at this time there; he must therefore be understood of a <ns0:hi>mystical Babylon.</ns0:hi> And the sense must be this, <ns0:hi>Come out,</ns0:hi> and be ye <ns0:hi>separate</ns0:hi> from those with whom your Souls will be in as much danger as the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> were in the literal <ns0:hi>Babylon.</ns0:hi> But whether by these are to be under<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stood <ns0:hi>Idolaters</ns0:hi> only, or all notorious scandalous Livers, is the question. The true determination of which, I conceive, de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pendeth upon the sense of those words, <ns0:hi>Come ye out, Be ye se<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />parate.</ns0:hi> Which words, I think, are not fully interpreted by those that follow, <ns0:hi>Touch not the unclean thing</ns0:hi>; for, doubtless, the former words are a Precept concerning the means to be used in order to that as an end; it being an hard thing to touch pitch, and not to be defiled therewith. On the other side, they interpret it too rigidly, who make it to be a prohibition of all Commerce, or company with such persons; for this is contrary to the Apostolical Doctrine in his former Epistle to this Church, where he had allowed, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 5. a civil Commerce and Traffick with the worst of men; and <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 7. had forbid<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />den the separation of Christians and Heathens, once joined in Marriage, unless the Unbeliever first departed. The Text therefore must be understood only of <ns0:hi>Elective,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>unnecessary, intimate Communion</ns0:hi>; and is much the same with that, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 14. <ns0:hi>be ye not unequally yoked with Vnbelievers.</ns0:hi> So as that it doth by no means justifie the withdrawing of all civil or religious Communion from those whose judgments or practice in all things we cannot approve; it only justifieth our withdrawing our communion from Idolaters, and from notorious scandalous Sinners in such duties and actions, or in such degrees, as we are under no obligation to have fellowship and communion with them in. And our forbearing to touch their <ns0:hi>unclean things</ns0:hi> in that fellowship and communion, which we are allowed with them, having no fellowship with them in their unfruitful works of darkness, but reproving them, even while in ci<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>il things, and some religious actions, we have some fellowship with them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Rev. 21.7.</ns0:note> will be a Father unto you, and ye shall be my sons and daughters, saith the Lord Al<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mighty <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">The latter words, which are a promise of Gods reception of them who for his sake withdraw from a sinful Communion with Idolaters, and scandalous persons, are taken out of <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 31.1, 9. and teach us this, That none can reasonably expect that God should fulfil his Covenant with them, who make no conscience of fulfilling their part in it with him; nor claim the benefits of a Father, who perform not the duties of his Chil<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dren: but on the contrary, those who are conscientious in the discharge of their duties of filial obedience, may expect from him both the kindness and the protection of a Father, (which is the more valuable, because he is the <ns0:hi>Lord God Al<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mighty,</ns0:hi> who wants no power to protect them, or so to in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fluence them, as to make them in all things happy, as the Children of so great a Father.)</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
